http://localhost/about-samurai.title: About Samurai
http://localhost/about-samurai.content: Samurai is a modern, intuitive Computerised Maintenance Management System designed to help you manage assets, schedule maintenance, and streamline workflows. It brings clarity to maintenance operations, helping teams reduce downtime, stay compliant, and make data-driven decisions with ease.

http://localhost/getting-started.title: Getting Started with Samurai
http://localhost/getting-started.content: Use this demo-content to familiarize yourself with Typemill. Not sure where to start? Simply select a topic in the navigation; it will briefly explain what you can do with Typemill.

http://localhost/getting-started/login-t.title: Login to Samurai
http://localhost/getting-started/login-t.content: To create a new page in Typemill, follow these steps: * Use the interactive navigation located on the left side of the screen.  * Enter a page title for your new page into one of the grey input fields. * Click the page icon to create a new page. You can also create a folder if you want to add sub-pages later. Here's a quick breakdown of the options. * Folders: Use folders to organize your website hierarchically. Folders can contain subfolders or pages. Unlike a traditional file system, folders in Typemill can also have content, similar to pages. * Pages: Utilize pages for simple content without needing a deeper structure. Additionally, you can rearrange your pages by dragging and dropping them within the navigation panel.

http://localhost/work-management/workord.title: WorkOrders
http://localhost/work-management/workord.content: Work Orders are at the heart of Samurai CMMS. They document every maintenance job that needs to be completed, whether it’s a routine inspection, a repair, or a one-off service request. Each work order helps you plan, assign, track, and record maintenance activities in a consistent and auditable way. A work order typically includes details such as: - Task information: what needs to be done and any specific instructions   - Asset and location: which equipment or area the job applies to   - Priority and due date: to help schedule and manage workloads   - Assigned personnel: the technician or team responsible for completing the task   - Parts and materials: what resources are required for the job   - Completion notes: what was done, time taken, and any follow-up actions needed   Work Orders can be created manually, generated automatically from recurring maintenance schedules, or raised through service requests submitted by staff. Once active, each work order moves through its lifecycle — open, in progress, and completed — giving you visibility over every stage of your maintenance process. By managing work orders in Samurai, your organisation gains: - Better control over maintenance planning and execution   - Clear visibility of work history and costs   - Consistent record keeping for compliance and audits

http://localhost/work-management/workord.title: Create a Work Order
http://localhost/work-management/workord.content: Desktop To create a Work Order in the Deskltop App, follow these steps. 1. From the side menu, select Work Management - Work Orders 1. Select + Add Work Order 1. Add a Title for the work order that briefly describes the work 1. Add an option description of the work 1. Select an Asset or Area. (An Asset or Area must be selected to open a Work Order) 1. Save the new Work Order ! The work order will save and then reopen providing more options. Once saved, a work order is automatically assigned a Work Order Number.

http://localhost/work-management/workord.title: Work Order Information
http://localhost/work-management/workord.content: The minimum information needed to create a work order is a title and selection of an Asset or Area, more information can be added to the work order. This section describes the other information that can be collected on a Work Order.  Compliance Task Flagging a Work Order as a Compliance Task, communicates that there is a legal requirement to complete this task. The Compliance Task flag is used in reporting to ensure assets have legally required work completed in a timely manner.  Work Order Status The Work Order status is used to track Work Orders as they progress. | Status | Description |  |:---|:---| | Open | The Work Order has been raised. |  | In Progress | The Work Order is currently being executed. |  | Complete | All work on the Work Order has been completed. |  | On Hold | The work on the Work Order has been paused. |  | Cancelled | The work order will not be completed. | When raising a Work Order on the desktop for new work, it will typically be raised ion the default Open status. The mobile App is where technicians can pick upn the open Work Orders, execute the work and update the status to In Progress and Complete as the work progresses.  Task Type
